title: Bringing a game port to Switch and New 3DS

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: How do you run the same game on a Switch and on a New 3DS?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That's the question behind this fork of sm64coopdx, the co-op version of Super Mario 64. Antoine explores both consoles as targets.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Do you rewrite the whole game for each?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: No. The shared game and co-op code sit on top, and the graphics, audio and input live behind platform-specific layers. Each console only has to fill in those layers.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Nice and tidy. Anything to check the hardware side?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes, a small platform probe, a lighter executable than the full game, to test things on the device. The work is mostly low-level C, aimed at tuning networking and memory use for handheld consoles, and the upstream project is credited. The written page has the structure.
